facts.fact: The World Bank states that civil registration in Mali is principally paper-based and decentralized in its current form, with paper records lacking systematic backup copies and no digital link possible to other legal ID systems, while digitization of civil registration processes is under development; no date is given, so the document's 2023 date is used.

The World Bank states that the civil registration system is managed jointly by local governments and the Ministry of Territorial Administration and Decentralization, with local governments handling birth registration; no date is given, so the document's 2023 date is used.

The World Bank states that the government adopted a national civil registration strategy in 2018; its reference list gives it as the National Civil Registration Strategy (2018-2022) of the Ministry of Territorial Administration and Decentralization, dated 20 July 2018, alongside a 2019 Master Plan of the Information System of the Civil Registry.

The World Bank states that, despite support from partners, a large financing gap remains for implementing the 2018 national civil registration strategy; it names no domestic budget line and no amount, and gives no date, so the document's 2023 date is used.

note: The same document also lists a 'civil registration register' among registers currently digitized, without description, which sits beside its statement that civil registration is principally paper-based. It gives a birth registration rate of 87 per cent, a share of births and not of offices, and says a certificate is obtained in person at the centre where the birth was declared.
